one_line_contribution: A manufactured procedure shift on ALFWorld (an 'activate' precondition before heat/cool/clean) is used to build a stale/fresh x weights/context factorial so that a QLoRA-trained procedure and a retrieved trajectory prescribe different actions for the same task, and the paper asks which substrate the agent's first decision follows — then converts the answer into a routing/cost claim that eviction, not retraining, sets a hybrid's post-shift recovery.
closest_prior_work: The Compliance Trap, arXiv:2607.10608 (verified via s2cli, 2026-07-12): its Enter-Propagation-Recovery framework already establishes that agents adopt task-wrong retrieved memory at the first exposed decision point and recover weakly, which is the entire W_none column of this proposal's 4x4 (C_none/C_pre/C_post/decoy at the entry point, with recovery and steps-to-recovery as the same estimands). The genuine increment is only the W_post/W_cont rows. On the other flank, the context-vs-parametric outcome is already the settled finding of the QA literature: arXiv:2506.06485 (verified) shows contextual conflict is disruptive and internal reliance hard to suppress, arXiv:2503.15888 (CK-PLUG, returned by search) tunes the reliance knob, and arXiv:2407.13048 'Establishing Knowledge Preference in Language Models' (returned by search Q4, not individually verified) explicitly fine-tunes preference orderings over parametric vs contextual vs instruction knowledge. The proposal's defence — those are pretrained facts in QA, not experimenter-trained procedures in an agent — is real but thin, because the QA result is precisely that freshly-injected parametric content loses to an explicit in-context statement. arXiv:2608.04574 'When Memory Lies' (verified) is the nearest agent-side staleness-conflict study (stale spatial memory vs contradicting observation, FrozenLake), but it has no trained-weights arm. Prior work therefore does not scoop the factorial, but it makes P1's direction close to a foregone conclusion.
strongest_objection: The headline finding is either pre-determined or confounded, and there is no dose ladder on the weights side to tell which. (1) Pre-determined: entry-point compliance is measured at the FIRST heat/cool/clean decision, i.e. before the environment has emitted a single 'Nothing happens.' At that moment the agent holds an exact, same-task, same-object demonstration of the old procedure in context versus a diffuse rank-32 LoRA prior over ~800 tasks. Asking whether the demonstration wins is close to asking whether ICL works; P1's non-inferiority form (CDI within 10 points of the no-weights arm) makes 'nothing happens' the confirmatory outcome. (2) Confounded: the proposal varies staleness on the context side with a randomized s in {0,1,2,3} ladder but holds the weights arm at a single point (QLoRA rank 32, 2 epochs, 55% of E_post). The conclusion 'the useful lever is eviction, not retraining' is therefore a statement about one LoRA hyperparameter setting, not about substrates; a reviewer will ask for the symmetric ladder (epochs / rank / target-pool fraction) and note that a stronger parametric arm could flip P1 and with it P5 and P7. (3) A concrete internal contradiction in the gates: Gate 0d wants the k=0 post-rule agent to fail on the shifted types (<=20% success), while Gate 0a wants stale context to cost >=6 net points of success relative to that same no-context cell. Since the shifted types are exactly the ones where the k=0 agent already times out, success(W_none, C_none) is likely single-digit and there is no room to lose 6 points — and the pre-registered fallback (strengthen the rule so activation must follow placement) pushes that cell further toward the floor, making Gate 0a harder rather than easier. The passable window is roughly success(C_none) in [6,20], which is narrow and unargued. (4) Two predictions are not predictions: P7 ('eviction costs zero GPU-hours, retraining costs >=0.3 GPU-h per block') is arithmetic, and P5 is close to entailed once Gate 0a holds and a FIFO bank of capacity 200 is flushed by a 200-task block — which is the same definitional objection that sank opposite_sided_failure_under_shift, reframed as a horse race rather than removed. (5) P6 is below the design's own resolution: it predicts >=5 net points of off-stream erosion while the Risk section states that with two probe types 'erosion below ~7 net points is not resolvable'; P3's equivalence claim on a slope ratio (two slopes within 40%) from four rungs is likewise not resolvable at +/-6.5 net per cell.
what_would_fix_it: Move the headline off the entry point and onto the part of the design that is not pre-determined: post-feedback recovery. 'Fresh weights do not even help the agent recover after the environment says Nothing happens' is a surprising claim; 'the in-context demonstration wins the first move' is not. Second, add the missing symmetric ladder: a weights-strength axis (0.5/1/2/4 epochs, or 10/30/100% of the post-rule target pool, or rank 8/32/128) crossed with C_pre, and report whether any reachable parametric strength buys protection — without it the routing conclusion cannot be stated as a substrate property, and the Pareto plot in P7 has one point on the retraining axis. Third, repair the Gate-0 window by measuring the manufactured harm on a metric that is not floor-bound (entry-point compliance and steps-to-recovery, with success secondary), and state the required range for success(W_none, C_none) explicitly, since Gate 0a and Gate 0d bracket it from opposite sides. Fourth, honour the brief's procedure-held-out rule: the T/B/H partition is by task id, so every evaluated procedure is in the training targets; hold out one entire shifted type from both E_post targets and the bank and report the conflict there. Fifth, either drop P6 or add probe types until the design resolves 5 net points, and replace P3's 40% slope-ratio equivalence with a directly powered contrast. Sixth, cut the factorial to fit: decoy needs to cross only W_none and W_post, not all four weights arms, which frees roughly 1,500 episodes for the ladder.
missing_baseline: A one-line rule-statement prompt arm: put 'you must issue activate <receptacle> before heat/cool/clean' in the system prompt, crossed with C_pre and W_pre. The manufactured shift is a single sentence, so this costs zero GPU-hours and ~15 tokens and, if it repairs the stale-context cells, it dominates both levers the paper is costing and the P7 Pareto plot becomes uninformative — the finding would be 'a sentence beats eviction beats retraining', not 'eviction beats retraining'. The critique-prompt variant ('verify memory against observations') is not a substitute, since it tests self-checking rather than stating the rule. A second omission on the same axis: recency-weighted or timestamp-filtered retrieval as the non-destructive alternative to FIFO eviction, which is the standard fix in the stale-retrieval literature (cf. arXiv:2606.26511 on temporal validity, in the novelty card); the stream arms contrast unbounded vs bounded-FIFO only, so 'the bank's eviction policy is the lever' is tested against one eviction policy. Third, the brief's mandated procedure-held-out (whole-task-type) split is absent.

Judging the proposal's own check: it is above average for this round — it names its queries, gives IDs, states the channel, and reports that WebSearch was unavailable rather than pretending to coverage it did not have. Its weakness is that all three queries sit on the agent-memory side; none searched the knowledge-injection/fine-tuning side, which is where the real threat to novelty lives, and my Q4 found exactly that (2407.13048, 2503.15888, 2405.05904 — freshly-injected parametric content losing to explicit context is a documented QA-side result). So the check is honest but one-sided, and the novelty argument it supports ('no agent-level result') is narrower than the proposal's framing implies.
